walkthroughs.body_html:
WWI began in August 1914 and ended on 11 November 1918.

On the Western Front, armies dug in. Trench warfare meant mud, machine guns, barbed wire and slow gains.

WWII began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

Hitler's Blitzkrieg swept through Poland, France and the Low Countries. War became global with Pearl Harbor in December 1941.

The Allies (Britain, France, USSR, USA) faced the Axis (Germany, Italy, Japan).

Key turning points: Stalingrad (1942-43), D-Day (June 1944), and the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945.

options: Belgian resistance delayed the German advance; Russia mobilised faster than expected; Moltke weakened the right wing; and the French rallied at the Marne.

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
